doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Choosing trumpet and hearing Louis Armstrong
summary: His first instrument was alto horn; he bought a trumpet and was hooked by an Armstrong record in Buffalo.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Why did you choose the trumpet?

Well my first instrument was the upright alto horn, because it was available in the family, it was in the house. And I didn’t dig it man, you know, um pah, um pah, pah-pah-pah. And I wanted to play the trumpet and I saved my pennies and my first trumpet I bought for $35 and got into it. And then I played trumpet in the high school band and then the way my interests broadened, I was walking down the street in Buffalo as a teenager, in the ‘30s, and I heard this sound of this trumpet and I couldn’t believe it. And I pushed through the crowd to follow the sound, and the source was a crank-up recording machine, a young lady was playing the old 78s. And I said, “What’s the name of that?” I thought it was a radio. I said, “What’s the name of that orchestra?” She didn’t know. She took it off and looked at it. And she said, “That’s Louis Armstrong.” I said, “I’d like to buy that.” And I did. And there you go. That started the whole thing. And when I played the record at home my whole family, who knew nothing of jazz, loved it. So that’s how he could communicate.
I guess so. I mean I’ve heard that story before. So he certainly had a large effect.
